It's a bit inconsistent that the function is called `get_vertex_count` but it's bound as `get_point_count`

I think this would need further revamping in the future.
The existing methods for getting vertex counts in different places is `get_vertex_count`, which makes sense.
But a lot of the vertex-manipulation methods use the term "point":
- move_point
- get_point_global_position
- get_point_transform

which is why I went with that naming.
I will rename my specific usages of "vertex" to "point" since that's what the other exposed methods use. I can also create a follow-up issue if we need to keep track of this naming inconsistency for further cleanup in the future?

`surface_get_array_index_len` seems to be getting all points, including what I'm assuming is overlapping points

Right, yeah, I was sure that `SoftBody3D` indices mapped to the index buffer and not the vertex buffer, but when looking at the code I think I mixed it up with the merging of vertices (not indices) that happen under the hood, where overlapping visual vertices will be merged into a single physics vertex.

So even with `surface_get_array_len` you won't get the true count of distinct soft body points, meaning `set_point_pinned(0, true)` and `set_point_pinned(42, true)` could end up pinning the same underlying physics point.

Anyway, that's more of an implementation detail I guess, the appropriate thing to return here is indeed the mesh's vertex buffer size, as that's what the various index parameters will be bounds-checked against.

Apologies for the mix-up.

I should have caught this the first time around, but from what I can tell almost all counts exposed through Godot's script bindings are `int` rather than `uint32_t`. I'm not sure if there's a good reason for this, or if it's purely by convention. Either way, I suggest we adhere to it.

```suggestion
	int get_point_count() const;
```

I believe this should be set to `PROPERTY_USAGE_NONE`, otherwise it'll show up as a (revertible) property in the inspector, and end up being serialized as well.

```suggestion
	ADD_PROPERTY(PropertyInfo(Variant::INT, "point_count", PROPERTY_HINT_NONE, "", PROPERTY_USAGE_NONE), "", "get_point_count");
```

You'll need to regenerate the documentation again after this change, as the default value in the documentation goes away.

The `-1` case I stumbled upon was this: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/320e81846979bd716341e0669231954543c4afbd/scene/resources/mesh.cpp#L1927-L1930 From what I can tell, not having any surfaces in the mesh will cause a massive cascade of other errors anyway, so I'm not sure it's super relevant here, but you can create custom `Mesh`-derived classes that might return negative values for other reasons as well. I'd say it's fine as-is.
